headline: Nvidia sheds 8% of its Huang rebound as Anthropic slips below IPO price
bottomLine: Nvidia gave back 8% of Monday's 31% rebound as Congress readied new China chip limits, and Anthropic fell below its $83 IPO price. SpaceX and Tesla named merger directors, Erebor passed $1B in loans, and Hormuz tanker attacks held oil near $89.

portfolio.title: SpaceX and Tesla name merger directors as Dec. 8 share unlock nears
portfolio.brief: FT: five directors will negotiate; Morgan Stanley and Goldman advise SpaceX, Evercore advises Tesla, and the share-exchange ratio is unsettled. Up to 797.6M SPCX shares can be sold from Dec. 8.
portfolio.impact: The ratio will decide what our remaining stake becomes, and the unlock may hit before it is set, leaving the stock to trade on rumor. Talks are FT-sourced; no deal is signed.
portfolio.action: Confirm with the fund team today whether the first-20% sale ran before the ~Nov 6 window, and decide the plan for the Dec. 8 unlock by Dec. 1.

portfolio.title: States sue SpaceX over Grok sexual images; xAI fights California AI law
portfolio.brief: Oregon and Virginia allege misleading Grok safety claims over sexualized images of real people, including minors, and seek penalties and injunctions. xAI also asks an appeals court to block California's AI disclosure law.
portfolio.impact: Judges sounded skeptical of xAI in the California case, and two states now test liability for Grok's output. Legal headlines will land just as the Dec. 8 unlock adds supply.
portfolio.action: Ask SpaceX investor relations this week for its legal-exposure estimate on the Grok suits, and get our counsel's read before Dec. 8 unlock decisions.

portfolio.title: Erebor passes $1B in loans, lends Harbinger over $100M with Pinegrove
portfolio.brief: FT: Erebor has topped $1B in loans against about $7B in deposits; the NY Post puts assets near $8B. With Pinegrove it is lending truck maker Harbinger over $100M, and it lent Forward Industries $50M.
portfolio.impact: Loans are a small slice of deposits, so earnings hinge on lending faster without credit mistakes. Harbinger and Forward are the first read on credit quality under the charter model.
portfolio.action: Make the Erebor introduction Circuit requested by Friday, and ask Erebor for its loan-book breakdown by borrower type and its target loan-to-deposit ratio.

portfolio.title: Perplexity says it hit $1B revenue, launches Monitor API; Amazon suit continues
portfolio.brief: NDTV (Nov. 18) reports Perplexity hit $1B in revenue; the basis isn't stated. Its new Monitor API runs continuous web watches, and Amazon wants to continue its suit over the AI tool in lower court.
portfolio.impact: If the revenue figure holds, it backs the agent-infrastructure push. The Amazon case tests whether AI agents may act on third-party sites, and a loss could limit where they operate.
portfolio.action: Ask Aravind Srinivas this week for the basis of the $1B figure (annualized or booked) and status of the NVIDIA-round confirmation we are waiting on.

portfolio.title: Air Force awards Anduril counter-air launcher prototype as stopgap fight looms
portfolio.brief: The Air Force gave Anduril a prototype contract for a counter-air missile launcher (ExecutiveBiz, Nov. 18). The White House wants stopgap-bill exemptions for Golden Dome and the Pentagon's munitions ramp-up.
portfolio.impact: A prototype award is a first step, not a production order, and a stopgap without exemptions can freeze new starts. The White House request helps only if Congress approves it.
portfolio.action: Ask Anduril's finance lead by Friday which programs, including this launcher, need stopgap exemptions to start, and whether production decisions slip if Congress refuses.

thesis.title: Trump says he 'made the deal' to bring back Nvidia's Huang
thesis.brief: Trump told CNBC he spoke to Nvidia's board and 'convinced them'; the board cited input from senior U.S. officials when it reversed course. Lawmakers from both parties want to know what was promised.
thesis.impact: A president overturning a chipmaker's board within days is the sudden executive action we described. The bipartisan backlash shows the contest is now fought in Washington, not in the market.

thesis.title: Dollar strength and bitcoin outflows cut against our debasement call
thesis.brief: Dollar Index held above 104, highest since March 2025; November bitcoin ETF outflows hit a record $4.71B. Strategy bought just 457 BTC ($29.6M), and an estimate puts its equity near 0.7x its bitcoin.
thesis.impact: Savers are buying dollars, not hard assets, and the largest corporate bitcoin buyer is slowing, so near-term evidence runs against sovereign rotation. The end-2027 G20 call is untested.

thesis.title: Nuclear wins a permit and Senate bill, but utilities still add gas for data centers
thesis.brief: TVA holds the first SMR construction permit but hasn't decided to build, and signed a $1.7B data-center deal. FirstEnergy won approval for a $2.5B gas plant; the Senate passed a permitting bill with nuclear amendments.
thesis.impact: Nuclear is advancing in permitting, yet utilities still add gas for data-center load, and Vistra's CEO calls interconnect queues overstated. The shift is real but slower than our call implies.

regulation.title: Congress readies tighter China chip limits as Huang is due to testify next week
regulation.brief: Bipartisan backlash makes new restrictions on Nvidia's China dealings more likely, and Huang is scheduled to testify in the Senate next week. The U.S. also added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist.
regulation.impact: Congress is likely to write the export limits the White House softened, keeping policy risk on AI-chip supply, which every compute-reliant portfolio company shares.
regulation.next: Huang testifies in the Senate next week; Nvidia's own probe remains open

regulation.title: South Korea proposes ending its ICO ban and limiting won stablecoins to banks
regulation.brief: The FSC's draft Digital Asset Act would allow domestic token sales under IPO-style disclosure and cap exchange ownership at 20%, with exceptions. Won stablecoins would start limited to bank-majority consortia.
regulation.impact: It reopens a large retail token market to onshore issuance, which favors tokens with disclosed revenue. Bank-led won stablecoins keep the payment rails with incumbents.
regulation.next: Draft awaits the legislative process; no vote date reported

tech.impact: An anonymous-staff scoop, not a company statement. If labs are holding back models, state action on frontier AI becomes likelier, the scenario in our Spiritual Warfare call.

macro.title: Anthropic shares fall below $83 IPO price days after listing
macro.brief: Anthropic traded below its $83 IPO price Tuesday, an early low about 27% under its first-day opening trade; Reuters says it is on track to lose nearly $200B in value.
macro.impact: The first frontier-lab IPO trading under water makes later AI listings and private rounds harder to price, a direct read-through for fundraising across our AI companies.
macro.action: Ask BlueNexus whether any bridge-round investor has asked to reprice since Anthropic fell below its IPO price, and finish our capital call this week.

macro.title: Three tankers hit within minutes in the Strait of Hormuz; oil near $89

macro.impact: Attacks during stalled talks point to a lasting supply shock, not a one-off spike. That keeps energy-security demand high for nuclear and distributed power, our Atomic Turn call.

frontier.title: China to fly its station's first international astronaut, from Pakistan
frontier.brief: China unveiled the Shenzhou-24 crew, with a Pakistani astronaut set to board Tiangong as its first international visitor. It also published its most detailed roadmap for a crewed Moon landing before 2030.
frontier.impact: A first for Tiangong and a sign China is building its own partner network beside the ISS. The flight is planned, not yet flown, and the Moon roadmap is a government plan.
